Yes, this feels right. I hit "Delete" and got a clear warning that named the exact bookmark and told me its saved copy would go too, with a way to back out ("Keep bookmark") right beside it. I confirmed and it was gone from the library. For something permanent like this, having it name what I'm about to lose and make me confirm is exactly the safeguard I'd want — I won't wipe something out by accident.

Now that we're clear this delete is truly permanent, it makes me realize there's a gentler cousin I'd also want. Sometimes I don't want to destroy a bookmark forever — I've dealt with it and want it out of my main list and out of my way, but I'd like to be able to get it back later if I change my mind. That's different from deleting. So I'd want a way to tuck a bookmark away — hidden from my everyday list but still kept — with somewhere I can go to see those put-away ones and pull one back if needed. Deleting stays the permanent option; this would be the reversible "set it aside for good, but keep it" option. Could we add that kind of put-away alongside delete?
